nodes.label: Allowlist expansion for opentargets/openfda (step 11)
nodes.rationale: api.platform.opentargets.org and api.fda.gov were added to the allowlist as human-approved edits during step 11 (RAG engine build) and live-verified, following the required human sign-off gate for any allowlist change.

nodes.label: Observability deferral rationale
nodes.rationale: Observability (OTel + SigNoz, step 15) was deferred until backend's src/ stabilizes, to avoid instrumenting code that is still changing.

nodes.label: k6 SLO thresholds
nodes.rationale: http_req_duration p95 <3000ms because query involves multi-source retrieval+grounding within the POC's latency budget; http_req_failed <1% because backend errors should be rare under normal load; escalation_rate <50% and insufficient_evidence_rate <30% are sanity bounds — a spike under load (given the fixed query mix) signals retrieval degrading, not harder questions, distinguishing a functional regression from expected behavior. These are POC-level bounds, not production SLOs.

nodes.label: Dual local/remote enforcement rationale
nodes.rationale: Hooks (local, Claude Code) and the MCP server (remote, any MCP client) both read the exact same data/allowlist/sources.json and data/schema/response_schema.json files, so there is exactly one source of truth for each, enforced two ways rather than duplicated and risking drift.

nodes.label: LLM provider-fallback mechanism
nodes.rationale: If the default LLM provider is unreachable/unconfigured, backend exposes POST /settings/provider-key to accept a user-supplied alternate provider API key (e.g. OpenRouter) for that session. The key is stored only at backend/.runtime/provider_key (gitignored) and never written to logs/responses.jsonl, .claude/audit/, triage reports, or any log line — protecting the secret while letting the session keep functioning.

nodes.label: Draft -> final triage report convention
nodes.rationale: p3-triage always writes first to reports/triage/<UTC-timestamp>-compliance-report.draft.md (ungated); only writing/renaming to the non-draft final filename when explicitly told to finalize, at which point human_gate.py intercepts that write for human approval before it's persisted — preventing an unreviewed compliance verdict from silently becoming official.

nodes.label: Context management for long-running subagents (plugin copy)
nodes.norm_label: context management for long-running subagents (plugin copy)
nodes.rationale: Rule: summarize everything older than the last 8-10 turns/prompts, capping the running summary at ~12-15% of the context window, and keep the most recent 8-10 turns verbatim — applied to p3-triage (reading prior finalized reports instead of re-deriving findings) and backend (summarizing earlier retrieval/grounding steps on long sessions) so subagent context stays bounded as logs grow without losing prior findings.

nodes.label: Domain routing reference (plugin copy)
nodes.rationale: Domain routing is agent-driven, not hardcoded: the backend classifies each question against the four evidence domains before retrieving, and retrieves only from domains that actually apply, because routing to only relevant domains keeps the allowlist check meaningful and avoids irrelevant citations diluting a claim's grounding. A single question may span multiple domains, but each resulting claim still carries exactly one evidence_domain tag.

nodes.label: Escalation decision table (plugin copy)
nodes.rationale: Weak or missing evidence never becomes a fabricated answer: it becomes insufficient_evidence (routine gap) or escalated (human weighs in because evidence bears on safety/clinical risk or is genuinely conflicting). escalation.required:true is caught by human_gate.py before the response is logged, so a human signs off before it reaches the team.

nodes.label: Four commitments (approved-sources, grounding, structured output, graceful failure)
nodes.norm_label: four commitments (approved-sources, grounding, structured output, graceful failure)
nodes.rationale: Each commitment is backed by a mechanical enforcement point rather than a convention: check_allowlist_retrieval.py hook gates retrieval; response_schema.json's citations minItems:1 makes an ungrounded claim structurally impossible; all responses must validate against the schema before being logged/shown; escalation-rules.md decision table forces weak/conflicting/blocked evidence to downgrade instead of being fabricated into an answer.

nodes.label: Finding: confidence heuristic counts URLs not distinct sources
nodes.norm_label: finding: confidence heuristic counts urls not distinct sources
nodes.rationale: grounding.py's corroboration-count heuristic counts distinct citation URLs, not distinct sources/hosts, so multiple hits from one client can inflate confidence to 'high' even though all citations are from a single host — contradicting the module docstring's 'independent allowlisted sources agreeing' semantics, and this inflated confidence can be the deciding factor in whether escalation triggers.

nodes.label: Finding: missing CORS middleware
nodes.rationale: main.py configures no CORS middleware, so the shipped frontend (served separately) cannot call the shipped backend cross-origin: POST /query's JSON content-type triggers a CORS preflight that fails without Access-Control-Allow-Origin, causing fetch() to throw even though the backend is reachable at the network layer.

nodes.label: Finding: dead-code re-validation in /query, real error path uncaught
nodes.norm_label: finding: dead-code re-validation in /query, real error path uncaught
nodes.rationale: main.py's belt-and-suspenders re-validation in /query is dead code because orchestrator.run_query() already validates and raises before returning; the real SchemaValidationError path propagates uncaught from an unguarded call site, producing a generic unhandled-exception 500 instead of the intended HTTPException(500) with schema-error detail.

nodes.label: Finding: escalation logic misses zero-result-without-block case
nodes.norm_label: finding: escalation logic misses zero-result-without-block case
nodes.rationale: orchestrator.py's _apply_escalation only handles the clinical+blocked partial-evidence case; when a requested domain returns zero results without being blocked while another domain succeeds, the response returns as 'answered' instead of 'insufficient_evidence', silently dropping an entire half of a multi-domain question while showing a fully-confident green banner — contradicting escalation-rules.md row 2.

nodes.label: Finding: server filesystem path leaks via escalation.reason
nodes.norm_label: finding: server filesystem path leaks via escalation.reason
nodes.rationale: AllowlistError messages embed the absolute server filesystem path (ALLOWLIST_PATH) and the full allowed-hosts list; these strings flow verbatim into escalation.reason returned by the API and rendered in the UI, leaking the server's absolute directory path (including local username) to any end user who triggers escalation on a blocked source.

nodes.label: Finding: frontend and backend both default to port 8000
nodes.norm_label: finding: frontend and backend both default to port 8000
nodes.rationale: frontend/README.md's suggested launch command (python3 -m http.server, default port 8000) and backend's default uvicorn invocation (no --port given, defaults to 8000) collide; whichever starts second fails to bind the port, and app.js's default API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000 ends up pointed at whichever server won the port.

nodes.label: Finding: unauthenticated provider-key endpoint, unrestricted file perms
nodes.norm_label: finding: unauthenticated provider-key endpoint, unrestricted file perms
nodes.rationale: POST /settings/provider-key has no authentication and stores the raw provider API key to disk without restrictive file permissions; any local process/user on a shared host can read another session's plaintext key, and any network client reaching the backend can overwrite the stored key for all users of that backend instance.

nodes.label: Finding: reload_allowlist() never called, stale lru_cache
nodes.norm_label: finding: reload_allowlist() never called, stale lru_cache
nodes.rationale: allowlist.py's reload_allowlist() exists to pick up a human-approved edit to sources.json but is never called anywhere; a running backend keeps serving a stale lru_cache'd allowlist, so a newly-approved host keeps raising AllowlistError until the process restarts, breaking the promised 'zero-code-change activation'.

nodes.label: Finding: javascript: URI XSS via unescaped citation href
nodes.norm_label: finding: javascript: uri xss via unescaped citation href
nodes.rationale: frontend/app.js's escapeAttr() only escapes double quotes before a citation URL is interpolated into an href attribute, so a javascript: URI citation is rendered as a live clickable link rather than neutralized; clicking such a citation link would execute attacker script in the page's origin.

nodes.label: Escalation decision table (generic template)
nodes.rationale: Weak or missing evidence never becomes a fabricated answer; replace 'high-stakes' with whatever the adopting domain's risk-bearing claim category is (in the pharma instance this template is based on: clinical/safety claims).

nodes.label: Genericization rationale for the scaffold
nodes.rationale: The scaffold extracts AIDLC's governance/agent-ops layer (hook + minItems:1 + escalation table mechanism) into a domain-agnostic reusable form: domain_a..domain_d replace the four pharma evidence domains (count isn't fixed at four), and only domain-specific wording in the skill/reference docs needs updating — the mechanism itself stays the same for any agentic app that needs approved-sources-only, grounded claims, structured output, and graceful failure.
